unit.why: One narrative: R. Yosef of Yampol, son of R. Michel of Zlotchov, is judged in the heavenly court for his prayers while gravely ill, on the same day his father dies; the Besht intercedes for him; a homiletic lesson follows.
unit.boundary_note: story ends with an ethical conclusion and source citation (נ״מ שביל אמונה ש״ג); previous division is a teaching on tefillin

stories.start_quote: כמו שאירע לבן הק׳ של הרב מוהר״ר מיכל
stories.end_quote: כי הם יבואו ממילא לתמים במעשיו וטוב לו בזה
stories.summary_en: While deathly ill, R. Yosef of Yampol ascends to the heavenly court, where an angel blows away his lifelong prayers. That same Sabbath his father, R. Michel of Zlotchov, dies in ecstatic devekut. The Besht, coming to greet R. Michel in heaven, has Yosef pray the morning prayer before the court; this prayer redeems all his earlier prayers, and he wakes healed.
